This is not the Copris the same site keeps on 24 septembrie, whom the corpus already holds: that one was born on the dung-heap beside the monastery of Theodosius the Cenobiarch in Palestine, and this line calls its man «Egipteanul». The two are separated here on the epithet and the day alone, and nothing else on this page bears on it.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 22.07.2026 (9. јул ст. ст.) — „Преп. Патермутије и Коприје“

attestations.note: The day’s fourth entry, the second of the two names its heading enumerates. The heading is quoted as the Prologue prints it, without a closing full stop, as every heading of this wave is. The Julian 9 July is the same menologion number this folder’s Romanian row carries, its only other venerated row, so there is no second day and no §4 note is owed. **WHICH OF THE DAY’S TWO PAIRS THIS FOLDER IS, AND THE SOURCE DECIDES IT.** doxologia’s line for 9 iulie is «Sfântul Cuvios Coprie Egipteanul», **Cuvios** — a venerable, not a martyr — and this folder’s `types` is `venerable` alone. Entry 3’s pair are Преп. муч., venerable-martyrs beheaded under Julian; entry 4’s are Преп., venerables who reposed at the end of the fourth century in deep old age, and „Обојица беху Мисирци“ stands over entry 3 while entry 4 keeps them Egyptians too. The rank is what settles it: **entry 4 is this folder’s entry.** **THE FIRST DATE OF ANY KIND THIS FOLDER HAS HELD, AND IT IS A CENTURY WITH A QUALIFIER.** `dates` was **null**, doxologia having printed the name and nothing more — no life, no troparion, no year, no place, no teacher. This book ends „Упокојили се у Господу крајем IV века, у дубокој старости“ — they reposed in the Lord at the end of the fourth century, in deep old age. The century is **stated**, not hedged, as Thomas of Maleon’s was on 7 July and unlike Lampadius’s „вероватно“ on 5 July, so it is written: `death` earliest 301, latest 400, display «end of the 4th century», basis traditional. **The interval is the whole century and not a narrower slice of it**, because «end of» is the book’s own qualifier and a boundary for it would be invented; it is kept in the display, where it is the source’s word, and not turned into numbers. **Deep old age is not a birth** and none is written. WHAT IS NEW IS EVERYTHING, THIS FOLDER HAVING HELD NO LIFE AT ALL. The entry is one entry for two men and most of its matter is the companion’s, and it is written as the entry’s: that the Patermuthius of this pair was first the leader of a band of robbers, converted by a wonderful vision — he had climbed onto the roof of a God-pleasing woman’s house to break in and plunder it, sleep fell on him, and in the sleep he saw Someone who threatened him to do evil no more and to repent, so that he was not only baptised but tonsured; that **both of them were great wonderworkers**, who by the grace of God healed people of every torment and sickness, turned sinners to the right way and prophesied; and the wonder of the three years, where a sinner on his deathbed begged for a longer life that he might repent, and after the prayer was told that God was adding three years, and repented, and died **exactly three years later**. `types` UNTOUCHED, AND **`wonderworker` IS REFUSED FOR THE SEVENTH TIME IN THIS RANGE.** `venerable` is there and „Преп.“ is exactly that word — the only rank this heading carries. „И један и други беху велики чудотворци“ stands in the **body**, and a rank read off a body is not written. No `office`, no `locations`: Egypt in one clause is not a coordinate. **NO NEW ROWS.** The folder already relates `theodosius-the-cenobiarch`, off the Romanian reading that kept it apart from the Copris of 24 septembrie, and this book does not name him. **ENTRY 4’S PATERMUTHIUS IS REFUSED FOR WANT OF A FOLDER, AND THE REFUSAL IS THE BOOK’S OWN.** He was first the leader of a band of robbers: he had climbed onto the roof of a God-pleasing woman’s house to get in and plunder it, sleep fell on him, and in the sleep he saw **Someone** who threatened him to do evil no more and to repent — so he was not only baptised but tonsured. With his companion he was a great wonderworker, healing every torment and sickness, turning sinners to the right way and prophesying; and a sinner on his deathbed begged him to lengthen his life that he might repent, and after the prayer the saint told him God was adding three years, and the sinner repented and died **exactly three years later**. `ls saints | grep -i patermuth` returns **three** and not one of them is he. `patermuthius-the-martyr` is «Patermuthius the Glorious», a `martyr` whose `death` is 305 to 311 under Maximian Galerius at the hands of Firmilian, kept with Elias on 17 September by three calendars — a martyr of a different persecution fifty years earlier. `patermuthius-17-december` is **entry 3’s man**, whom this very entry exists to tell entry 4’s apart from, so writing entry 4 onto him would be the exact error the Дула ruling forbids. `elias-martyr-with-patermuthius` is the companion of the first. Ruling 3: named here, left out of no life — his story is written into `copres-the-egyptian`’s life, the entry being one entry and the companion’s folder existing — but **no folder from me**, and **no row for any Patermuthius on entry 4**. The three years, the age and the end of the fourth century are written on Copres, whose entry they also are, and nowhere else. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion; the day carries only the verse. **THE DAY PRINTS THE SAME TWO NAMES TWICE AND SAYS OUTRIGHT THAT THE MEN ARE DIFFERENT.** Entry 3 is „Преп. муч. Патермутије и Коприје“ and entry 4 is „Преп. Патермутије и Коприје“, and entry 4 opens „Мада истих имена, ови беху различити од оних првих“ — though of the same names, these were different from the first ones. The standing ruling that **two commemorations on one calendar means two men** — which kept the Prologue’s Egyptian monk Дула off `doulas-of-cilicia` on 15 June — is here made by the book itself, in a sentence, and it decides four readings at once. Entry 3’s pair are Преп. муч., venerable-martyrs, beheaded under Julian the Apostate with a soldier Alexander, aged 75 and 45, in 361: that is `patermuthius-17-december` and `copris-17-december`, whose Greek rows stand on 17 December with `death` «between 361 and 363» off Julian’s reign and his Persian campaign, and who relate each other and `alexander-17-december` already. Entry 4’s pair are Преп., venerables and wonderworkers who reposed at the end of the fourth century in deep old age: doxologia keeps **one** of them on this very 9 July as «Sfântul Cuvios Coprie Egipteanul», `venerable`, which is `copres-the-egyptian` — and **entry 4’s Patermuthius has no folder at all**.

death.note: The folder’s first date of any kind; `dates` was null before this reading, doxologia having printed the name and nothing more — no life, no troparion, no year, no place, no teacher. The Охридски пролог for 9. јул ст. ст., fourth entry: „Упокојили се у Господу крајем IV века, у дубокој старости“ — they reposed in the Lord at the end of the fourth century, in deep old age. The century is stated and not hedged. **The interval is the whole century**, because «end of» is the book’s own qualifier and any narrower boundary would be invented; the qualifier is kept in the display, where it is the source’s word, and is not turned into numbers. Deep old age is not a birth and none is written. The three years God added to a dying sinner’s life in this entry are a duration and not a date (6 October 2026).
